Filesystem-supported finite mtime beyond the Go UnixNano interval preserves source stat().st_mtime: seconds plus fractional nanoseconds; the year-2300 file list and a subsequent ordinary timestamp recovery are source-bound.

Finite mtime preserves source two-step floating rounding: seconds plus float64(nanoseconds * 1e-9). An explicit intermediate conversion prevents fused multiply-add. Independent source cases include 3ns after epoch, -3ns, 2038, UnixNano overflow edge, year2300 and ordinary recovery; SDK list and shared metadata both compare complete source rows.

Unpaired JSON surrogate path tokens are rejected before UTF-8 replacement, including escaped-equivalent storage local; ordinary source returned missing false/[]/true but retained U+FFFD. This is an explicit filesystem encoding boundary, not equal return semantics.

Existing moduleTransferFloat constructor accepts a narrower ASCII finite modify_time grammar than all source Pydantic values. Arbitrary Unicode numeric/nonfinite metadata input is an open shared-constructor dependency, not claimed by this producer slice.

Native POSIX filenames that are not valid UTF-8 fail closed before FileItem JSON encoding. Source retains surrogate-escaped identity. The current protocol guarantees valid UTF-8 paths and does not implement an explicit byte-preserving encoding for native non-UTF8 names: never alias a native byte-FF filename to a distinct genuine U+FFFD file. This is a current safety boundary, not a claim that Go/JSON inherently cannot represent byte identity. Read-only tests retain both originals and verify the valid-name next operation.
